2026-08-12 — NO DRIFT, and one structural fix. Four rows were re-fetched from their primary source today and every one held: registry.npmjs.org/tearline is still HTTP 404 with "private": true in package.json, kyisaiah47/tearline is still PRIVATE, /tearline.js is still HTTP 200 at 14,048 bytes / 370 lines, and the served-size figure the four content pages carry is now on its third identical reading. The npm package rows, the spec-behaviour rows and the two Spotify rows were deliberately not re-fetched — they were all confirmed on 2026-08-09 or 2026-08-06 and none of them moves week to week.

THE CRAWL-STATE CLAIM IN sitemap.ts WAS STALE AND IS CORRECTED. That file has asserted "five of five subpages discovered" since 2026-08-08. Today's URL Inspection run reports six of seven URLs as "URL is unknown to Google": /docs, /dom-to-png, /receipt-ui and /share-image-custom-element have all gone back to unknown, and /spotify-receipt-generator is the only subpage still reading "Discovered - currently not indexed". Whether that is a regression or a transient earlier reading, the file was stating something the primary source contradicts, which is the one thing it must not do. Rewritten with today's measurement.

Two checks were run rather than assumed. First, kynth.studio was fetched (HTTP 200) and it does carry real crawlable <a href="https://tearline.kynth.studio"> links — a Selected Work card and the logo ticker — so the host is not orphaned and the standing "no inbound links" note was overstated. Second, and this is the finding: every link from the HOME PAGE to the five subpages lived in SiteFooter.tsx and nowhere else. The four content pages link to each other densely in prose, but sibling links carry nothing while the siblings are themselves uncrawled, and a sitewide boilerplate footer nav is the weakest inbound signal a page can have. That was the only signal / gave them.

FIXED, in InstallSection.tsx: four contextual prose links, one per content page, in visible body copy — not a related-posts strip, not the FAQ (whose answers sit in a collapsed accordion), and not another footer row. Each sits in the paragraph a reader would already be in when they want it: the foreignObject note now points at /dom-to-png, the upgrade-in-place note at /share-image-custom-element, the --ink/--paper accessibility note at /receipt-ui, and the usage snippet at /spotify-receipt-generator for the live-data case. The home page's sitemap lastModified moves to 2026-08-12 because its content actually changed; no other date moved.

NO PAGE SHIPPED, and none was needed — all six measured buyer queries still have an owned page. Today's competitor-gap domains were npmjs.com, stackoverflow.com, github.com and cdnjs.cloudflare.com. All four are third-party surfaces: npmjs.com is the registry these pages cite as a primary source, cdnjs is a CDN serving the same four packages /dom-to-png already compares, and Stack Overflow and GitHub have been dismissed on the same grounds for eleven runs. No owned comparison page closes any of them.

claims.value: published as @kynth/tearline (0.1.0, 2026-08-12); the hosted script tag remains an equally supported install path
claims.note:
RESOLVED 2026-08-12. Published as @kynth/tearline@0.1.0. The bare name `tearline` is NOT taken (registry.npmjs.org/tearline was still a clean 404) but it is UNREGISTERABLE: `npm publish` returns HTTP 403 "Package name too similar to existing package readline". That is npm's similarity/typo-squat filter, not a collision, and no amount of waiting changes it. The @kynth org already existed on the registry (it carries @kynth/api, @kynth/api-mcp, @kynth/ai-tools), so the scope preserves the product name exactly rather than mangling it to tearline-element or tear-line.

The published manifest is ops/npm/package.json, NOT the repo root package.json. The root manifest is the SITE's — it stays "private": true and it depends on next, react, posthog-js, lenis and sonner. Publishing it would have handed `npm i` six runtime dependencies against a package whose first line promises zero. The published package has zero dependencies and four files (tearline.js, README.md, LICENSE, package.json), 21.3 kB unpacked.

A REAL BUG WAS CAUGHT ON THE WAY. src/tearline.js — the file the root manifest's `main` pointed at — was 340 lines / 12,756 bytes, while public/tearline.js and the live origin were 370 lines / 14,048 bytes. The 2026-08-06 commit b76c925 that added the `tearline:stage` export events edited public/ only, so `main` had been two weeks stale and a naive publish would have shipped a component OLDER than the playground serves, silently. src/ has been synced from public/ (both now sha256 96debf4e…). ops/npm/publish.mjs is the gate that makes it unrepeatable: it fetches the live /tearline.js and REFUSES to publish unless the staged file, src/tearline.js and the origin are all the same bytes.

SURFACES STILL CARRYING THE OLD CLAIM. README.md, public/llms.txt and src/app/share-image-custom-element/page.tsx were corrected on 2026-08-12. The npm CTA has NOT been restored to SiteHeader.tsx, HeroSection.tsx, InstallSection.tsx, SiteFooter.tsx, page.tsx or docs/page.tsx — those rows were deliberately REMOVED on 2026-07-29 rather than reworded, and putting an `npm i` row back into the header, hero and install section is a copy and layout decision for Isaiah, not a factual patch. The explanatory code comments in those files (and in mobile.css, JsonLd.tsx, CommandButton.tsx) still say the package is unpublished and are now wrong; they are comments, not rendered copy.
